shloka_text: सुकेशं धार्मिकं दृष्ट्वा वरलब्धं च राक्षसम् । ग्रामणीर्नाम गन्धर्वो विश्वावसुसमप्रभः ।। 7.5.1 ।।
transliteration: sukeśaṃ dhārmikaṃ dṛṣṭvā varalabdhaṃ ca rākṣasam | grāmaṇīrnāma gandharvo viśvāvasusamaprabhaḥ || 7.5.1 ||
translation: सुकेशं Sukesha, धार्मिकं righteous, दृष्ट्वा having seen, वरलब्धं having obtained a boon, च and, राक्षसम् the demon, ग्रामणीर्नाम named Gramani, गन्धर्वो a Gandharva, विश्वावसुसमप्रभः having splendor like Vishvavasu.
explanation: Having seen Sukesha, the righteous demon who had obtained a boon, a Gandharva named Gramani, whose splendor was like that of Vishvavasu, (approached him).
comments: The Gandharva Gramani gives his daughter Devavati to Sukesha, who begets three mighty sons -- Malyavan, Sumali and Mali -- by severe penance they win from Brahma invincibility, long life and mutual devotion, and have Vishvakarma build them the city of Lanka on Trikuta -- wedding three Gandharva maidens they beget numerous rakshasa offspring, among them Kaikasi -- grown arrogant, the three brothers torment the gods, sages, nagas and yakshas.

shloka_text: तस्य देववती नाम द्वितीया श्रीरिवात्मजा । त्रिषु लोकेषु विख्याता रूपयौवनशालिनी । तां सुकेशाय धर्मेण ददौ रक्षःश्रियं यथा ।। 7.5.2 ।।
transliteration: tasya devavatī nāma dvitīyā śrīrivātmajā | triṣu lokeṣu vikhyātā rūpayauvanaśālinī | tāṃ sukeśāya dharmeṇa dadau rakṣaḥśriyaṃ yathā || 7.5.2 ||
translation: tasya his, devavatī Devavati, nāma named, dvitīyā second, śrīriva like Lakshmi, ātmajā daughter, triṣu in three, lokeṣu worlds, vikhyātā renowned, rūpayauvanaśālinī endowed with beauty and youth, tāṃ her, sukeśāya to Sukesha, dharmeṇa righteously, dadau gave, rakṣaḥśriyaṃ the prosperity of the Rakshasas, yathā just as.
explanation: He had a second daughter named Devavati, renowned in the three worlds for her beauty and youth, whom he righteously gave to Sukesha, just as one would bestow the prosperity of the Rakshasas.

shloka_text: वरदानकृतैश्वर्यं सा तं प्राप्य पतिं प्रियम् । आसीद्देववती तुष्टा धनं प्राप्येव निर्धनः ।। 7.5.3 ।।
transliteration: varadānakṛtaiśvaryaṃ sā taṃ prāpya patiṃ priyam | āsīddevavatī tuṣṭā dhanaṃ prāpyeva nirdhanaḥ || 7.5.3 ||
translation: varadānakṛtaiśvaryaṃ whose prosperity was made by boons, sā she, taṃ him, prāpya having obtained, patiṃ husband, priyam dear, āsīt became, devavatī Devavati, tuṣṭā pleased, dhanaṃ wealth, prāpya having obtained, iva as if, nirdhanaḥ a poor man.
explanation: Having obtained him, her dear husband whose prosperity was due to boons, Devavati became as pleased as a poor man who has acquired wealth.

shloka_text: स तया सह संयुक्तो रराज रजनीचरः । अञ्जनादभिनिष्क्रान्तः करेण्वेव महागजः ।। 7.5.4 ।।
transliteration: sa tayā saha saṃyukto rarāja rajanīcaraḥ | añjanādabhiniṣkrāntaḥ kareṇveva mahāgajaḥ || 7.5.4 ||
translation: sa he, tayā with her, saha together, saṃyuktaḥ united, rarāja shone, rajanīcaraḥ the night-wanderer, añjanāt from Anjana mountain, abhiniṣkrāntaḥ having emerged, kareṇvā with a female elephant, iva as if, mahāgajaḥ a great elephant.
explanation: United with her, that Rakshasa shone like a great elephant emerging from the Anjana mountain with a female elephant.

shloka_text: देववत्यां सुकेशस्तु जनयामास राघव ।। 7.5.5 ।।
transliteration: devavatyāṃ sukeśastu janayāmāsa rāghava || 7.5.5 ||
translation: devavatyāṃ in Devavati, sukeśaḥ Sukesha, tu indeed, janayāmāsa begot, rāghava O Raghava.
explanation: Indeed, Sukesha begot children in Devavati, O Raghava.

shloka_text: त्रीन् पुत्रान् जनयामास त्रेताग्निसमविग्रहान् । माल्यवन्तं सुमालिं च मालिं च बलिनां वरम् । त्रींस्त्रिनेत्रसमान्पुत्रान्राक्षसान्राक्षसाधिपः ।। 7.5.6 ।।
transliteration: trīn putrān janayāmāsa tretāgnisamavigrahān | mālyavantaṃ sumāliṃ ca māliṃ ca balināṃ varam | trīṃstrinetrasamānputrānrākṣasānrākṣasādhipaḥ || 7.5.6 ||
translation: trīn three, putrān sons, janayāmāsa begot, tretāgnisamavigrahān whose bodies were like the three sacred fires, mālyavantaṃ Malyavan, sumāliṃ Sumali, ca and, māliṃ Mali, ca and, balināṃ among the strong, varam the best, trīn three, trinetrasamān equal to the three-eyed one (Shiva), putrān sons, rākṣasān Rakshasas, rākṣasādhipaḥ the lord of Rakshasas.
explanation: The lord of Rakshasas begot three sons, Malyavan, Sumali, and Mali (the best among the strong), who were Rakshasas with bodies like the three sacred fires and equal to Shiva.

shloka_text: त्रयो लोका इवाव्यग्राः स्थितास्त्रय इवाग्नयः । त्रयो मन्त्रा इवात्युग्रास्त्रयो घोरा इवामयाः ।। 7.5.7 ।।
transliteration: trayo lokā ivāvyagrāḥ sthitāstraya ivāgnayaḥ | trayo mantrā ivātyugrāstrayo ghorā ivāmayāḥ || 7.5.7 ||
translation: त्रयः three, लोकाः worlds, इव like, अव्यग्राः undisturbed, स्थिताः stood, त्रयः three, इव like, अग्नयः fires, त्रयः three, मन्त्राः incantations, इव like, अत्युग्राः extremely fierce, त्रयः three, घोराः dreadful, इव like, आमयाः diseases
explanation: They remained like the three undisturbed worlds, like the three sacred fires, like three extremely fierce incantations, and like three dreadful diseases.

shloka_text: त्रयः सुकेशस्य सुतास्त्रेताग्निसमतेजसः । विवृद्धिमगमंस्तत्र व्याधयोपेक्षिता इव ।। 7.5.8 ।।
transliteration: trayaḥ sukeśasya sutāstretāgnisamatejasaḥ | vivṛddhimagamaṃstatra vyādhayopekṣitā iva || 7.5.8 ||
translation: त्रयः three, सुकेशस्य of Sukesha, सुताः sons, त्रेताग्निसमतेजसः having splendor equal to the three sacred fires, विवृद्धिम् growth, अगमन् attained, तत्र there, व्याधयः diseases, उपेक्षिताः neglected, इव like
explanation: The three sons of Sukesha, possessing a brilliance akin to the three sacred fires, grew there like neglected diseases.

shloka_text: वरप्राप्तिं पितुस्ते तु ज्ञात्वेश्वरतपोबलात् । तपस्तप्तुं गता मेरुं भ्रातरः कृतनिश्चयाः ।। 7.5.9 ।।
transliteration: varaprāptiṃ pituste tu jñātveśvaratapobalāt | tapastaptuṃ gatā meruṃ bhrātaraḥ kṛtaniścayāḥ || 7.5.9 ||
translation: वरप्राप्तिम् the obtaining of a boon, पितुः of their father, ते they, तु indeed, ज्ञात्वा having known, ईश्वरतपोबलात् from the power of Shiva's penance, तपः penance, तप्तुम् to perform, गताः went, मेरुम् to Mount Meru, भ्रातरः brothers, कृतनिश्चयाः having made a firm resolve
explanation: Having learned of their father's boon obtained through the power of Shiva's penance, the brothers, having made a firm resolve, went to Mount Meru to perform penance.

shloka_text: प्रगृह्य नियमान्घोरान्राक्षसा नृपसत्तम । विचेरुस्ते तपो घोरं सर्वभूतभयावहम् ।। 7.5.10 ।।
transliteration: pragṛhya niyamānghorānrākṣasā nṛpasattama | viceruste tapo ghoraṃ sarvabhūtabhayāvaham || 7.5.10 ||
translation: प्रगृह्य having undertaken, नियमान् vows, घोरान् terrible, राक्षसाः the Rakshasas, नृपसत्तम O best of kings, विचेरुः they performed, ते they, तपः penance, घोरम् terrible, सर्वभूतभयावहम् causing fear to all beings
explanation: O best of kings, those Rakshasas undertook severe vows and performed terrible penance that instilled fear in all beings.

shloka_text: सत्यार्जवशमोपेतैस्तपोभिरतिदुष्करैः । सन्तापयन्तस्त्रील्लोँकान्सदेवासुरमानुषान् ।। 7.5.11 ।।
transliteration: satyārjavaśamopetaistapobhiratiduṣkaraiḥ | santāpayantastrīlloँkānsadevāsuramānuṣān || 7.5.11 ||
translation: सत्यार्जवशमोपेतैः endowed with truth, straightforwardness, and self-control, तपोभिः by penances, अतिदुष्करैः extremely difficult to perform, सन्तापयन्तः causing distress, त्रीन् three, लोकान् worlds, सदेवासुरमानुषान् along with gods, asuras, and humans
explanation: Through their extremely difficult penances, which were endowed with truth, straightforwardness, and self-control, they tormented the three worlds, including gods, asuras, and humans.

shloka_text: ततो विभुश्चतुर्वक्त्रो विमानवरमास्थितः । सुकेशपुत्रानामन्त्र्य वरदो ऽस्मीत्यभाषत ।। 7.5.12 ।।
transliteration: tato vibhuścaturvaktro vimānavaramāsthitaḥ | sukeśaputrānāmantrya varado 'smītyabhāṣata || 7.5.12 ||
translation: ततः then, विभुः the powerful one (Brahma), चतुर्वक्त्रः four-faced, विमानवरम् the excellent aerial chariot, आस्थितः having ascended, सुकेशपुत्रान् the sons of Sukesha, आमन्त्र्य having addressed, वरदः a bestower of boons, अस्मि I am, इति thus, अभाषत spoke.
explanation: Then, the powerful, four-faced Brahma, seated on his excellent aerial chariot, addressed the sons of Sukesha, declaring, "I am here to grant boons."

shloka_text: ब्रह्माणं वरदं ज्ञात्वा सेन्द्रैर्देवगणैर्वृतम् । ऊचुः प्राञ्जलयः सर्वे वेपमाना इव द्रुमाः ।। 7.5.13 ।।
transliteration: brahmāṇaṃ varadaṃ jñātvā sendrairdevagaṇairvṛtam | ūcuḥ prāñjalayaḥ sarve vepamānā iva drumāḥ || 7.5.13 ||
translation: ब्रह्माणम् Brahma, वरदम् the bestower of boons, ज्ञात्वा having known, सेन्द्रैः with Indra, देवगणैः by hosts of gods, वृतम् surrounded, ऊचुः they spoke, प्राञ्जलयः with folded hands, सर्वे all, वेपमानाः trembling, इव like, द्रुमाः trees.
explanation: Realizing that Brahma, the bestower of boons, was present, surrounded by Indra and hosts of gods, all of them spoke with folded hands, trembling like trees.

shloka_text: तपसाराधितो देव यदि नो दिशसे वरम् । अजेयाः शत्रुहन्तारस्तथैव चिरजीविनः ।। 7.5.14 ।।
transliteration: tapasārādhito deva yadi no diśase varam | ajeyāḥ śatruhantārastathaiva cirajīvinaḥ || 7.5.14 ||
translation: तपसा by penance, आराधितः worshipped, देव O Lord, यदि if, नः to us, दिशसे you grant, वरम् a boon, अजेयाः unconquerable, शत्रुहन्तारः destroyers of enemies, तथैव and also, चिरजीविनः long-lived.
explanation: They requested, "O Lord, if you, who have been propitiated by our penance, grant us a boon, let us be unconquerable, destroyers of enemies, and also long-lived."

shloka_text: प्रभविष्ण्वो भवामेति परस्परमनुव्रताः ।। 7.5.15 ।।
transliteration: prabhaviṣṇvo bhavāmeti parasparamanuvratāḥ || 7.5.15 ||
translation: प्रभविष्ण्वः powerful, भवाम let us be, इति thus, परस्परम् mutually, अनुव्रताः devoted.
explanation: They further requested, "And let us be mighty, always devoted to each other."

shloka_text: एवं भविष्यतीत्युक्त्वा सुकेशतनयान्विभुः । स ययौ ब्रह्मलोकाय ब्रह्मा ब्राह्मणवत्सलः ।। 7.5.16 ।।
transliteration: evaṃ bhaviṣyatītyuktvā sukeśatanayānvibhuḥ | sa yayau brahmalokāya brahmā brāhmaṇavatsalaḥ || 7.5.16 ||
translation: एवम् thus, भविष्यति it shall be, इति thus, उक्त्वा having said, सुकेशतनयान् to the sons of Sukesha, विभुः the powerful one (Brahma), सः he, ययौ went, ब्रह्मलोकाय to the world of Brahma, ब्रह्मा Brahma, ब्राह्मणवत्सलः affectionate to Brahmins.
explanation: Having told the sons of Sukesha, "So it shall be," the powerful Brahma, who is affectionate to Brahmins, then returned to his own world.

shloka_text: वरं लब्ध्वा तु ते सर्वे राम रात्रिञ्चरास्तदा । सुरासुरान्प्रबाधन्ते वरदानसुनिर्भयाः ।। 7.5.17 ।।
transliteration: varaṃ labdhvā tu te sarve rāma rātriñcarāstadā | surāsurānprabādhante varadānasunirbhayāḥ || 7.5.17 ||
translation: वरं boon, लब्ध्वा having obtained, तु indeed, ते those, सर्वे all, राम O Rama, रात्रिञ्चराः night-wanderers, तदा then, सुरासुरान् gods and asuras, प्रबाधन्ते they harass, वरदानसुनिर्भयाः very fearless because of the boon.
explanation: O Rama, having obtained the boon, all those night-wanderers then became very fearless due to the boon and began to harass both gods and asuras.

shloka_text: तैर्वध्यमानास्त्रिदशाः सर्षिसङ्घाः सचारणाः । त्रातारं नाधिगच्छन्ति निरयस्था यथा नराः ।। 7.5.18 ।।
transliteration: tairvadhyamānāstridaśāḥ sarṣisaṅghāḥ sacāraṇāḥ | trātāraṃ nādhigacchanti nirayasthā yathā narāḥ || 7.5.18 ||
translation: तैः by them, वध्यमानाः being tormented, त्रिदशाः the gods, सर्षिसङ्घाः along with groups of sages, सचारणाः along with Charanas, त्रातारं a protector, न not, अधिगच्छन्ति they find, निरयस्थाः those in hell, यथा just as, नराः people.
explanation: Being tormented by them, the gods, along with groups of sages and Charanas, could not find a protector, just like people suffering in hell.

shloka_text: अथ ते विश्वकर्माणं शिल्पिनां वरमव्ययम् । ऊचुः समेत्य संहृष्टा राक्षसा रघुसत्तम ।। 7.5.19 ।।
transliteration: atha te viśvakarmāṇaṃ śilpināṃ varamavyayam | ūcuḥ sametya saṃhṛṣṭā rākṣasā raghusattama || 7.5.19 ||
translation: अथ then, ते those, विश्वकर्माणं to Vishwakarma, शिल्पिनां of artisans, वरं the best, अव्ययम् imperishable, ऊचुः they said, समेत्य having met, संहृष्टाः delighted, राक्षसाः the Rakshasas, रघुसत्तम O best of Raghu's lineage.
explanation: O best of Raghu's lineage, then those delighted Rakshasas, having met Vishwakarma, the best and imperishable among artisans, spoke to him.

shloka_text: ओजस्तेजोबलवतां महतामात्मतेजसा । गृहकर्ता भवानेव देवानां हृदयेप्सितम् ।। 7.5.20 ।।
transliteration: ojastejobalavatāṃ mahatāmātmatejasā | gṛhakartā bhavāneva devānāṃ hṛdayepsitam || 7.5.20 ||
translation: ओजः vigor, तेजः splendor, बलवतां of the powerful, महतां of the great, आत्मतेजसा by your own splendor, गृहकर्ता the house-builder, भवान् you, एव alone, देवानां of the gods, हृदयेप्सितम् desired by the heart.
explanation: You alone, by your own splendor, are the cherished house-builder for the great, vigorous, splendid, and powerful gods.

shloka_text: अस्माकमपि तावत्त्वं गृहं कुरु महामते । हिमवन्तमपाश्रित्य मेरुमन्दरमेव वा । महेश्वरगृहप्रख्यं गृहं नः क्रियतां महत् ।। 7.5.21 ।।
transliteration: asmākamapi tāvattvaṃ gṛhaṃ kuru mahāmate | himavantamapāśritya merumandarameva vā | maheśvaragṛhaprakhyaṃ gṛhaṃ naḥ kriyatāṃ mahat || 7.5.21 ||
translation: अस्माकम् for us, अपि also, तावत् therefore, त्वं you, गृहं a house, कुरु make, महामते O great-minded one, हिमवन्तम् the Himalayas, अपाश्रित्य having resorted to, मेरुमन्दरम् Meru or Mandara, एव indeed, वा or, महेश्वरगृहप्रख्यं resembling the dwelling of Maheswara, गृहं a house, नः for us, क्रियतां let it be made, महत् great.
explanation: O great-minded one, therefore, please build a grand dwelling for us also, resembling the abode of Maheswara, either by resorting to the Himalayas or Mount Meru or Mandara.

shloka_text: विश्वकर्मा ततस्तेषां राक्षसानां महाभुजः । निवासं कथयामास शक्रस्येवामरावतीम् ।। 7.5.22 ।।
transliteration: viśvakarmā tatasteṣāṃ rākṣasānāṃ mahābhujaḥ | nivāsaṃ kathayāmāsa śakrasyevāmarāvatīm || 7.5.22 ||
translation: विश्वकर्मा Vishwakarma, ततः then, तेषां to them, राक्षसानां of the Rakshasas, महाभुजः the mighty-armed, निवासं dwelling place, कथयामास described, शक्रस्य of Indra, इव like, अमरावतीम् Amaravati.
explanation: Then, the mighty-armed Vishwakarma described to those Rakshasas a dwelling place, which was like Amaravati, the city of Indra.

shloka_text: दक्षिणस्योदधेस्तीरे त्रिकूटो नाम पर्वतः । सुवेल इति चाप्यन्यो द्वितीयस्तत्र सत्तमाः ।। 7.5.23 ।।
transliteration: dakṣiṇasyodadhestīre trikūṭo nāma parvataḥ | suvela iti cāpyanyo dvitīyastatra sattamāḥ || 7.5.23 ||
translation: दक्षिणस्य of the southern, उदधेः ocean, तीरे on the shore, त्रिकूटो Trikuta, नाम named, पर्वतः mountain, सुवेल Suvela, इति thus, च and, अपि also, अन्यः another, द्वितीयः second, तत्र there, सत्तमाः O best ones.
explanation: O best ones, on the shore of the southern ocean, there is a mountain named Trikuta, and another, a second one, named Suvela.

shloka_text: शिखरे तस्य शैलस्य मध्यमे ऽम्बुदसन्निभे । शकुनैरपि दुष्प्रापे टङ्कच्छिन्नचतुर्दिशि ।। 7.5.24 ।।
transliteration: śikhare tasya śailasya madhyame 'mbudasannibhe | śakunairapi duṣprāpe ṭaṅkacchinnacaturdiśi || 7.5.24 ||
translation: शिखरे on the peak, तस्य of that, शैलस्य mountain, मध्यमे middle, अम्बुदसन्निभे cloud-like, शकुनैः by birds, अपि even, दुष्प्रापे difficult to reach, टङ्कच्छिन्नचतुर्दिशि carved on all four sides with a chisel.
explanation: On the middle peak of that mountain, which resembles a cloud, is difficult for even birds to reach, and is carved on all four sides as if by a chisel.

shloka_text: त्रिंशद्योजनक्स्तीर्णा शतयोजनमायता । स्वर्णप्राकारसंवीता हेमतोरणसंवृता ।। 7.5.25 ।।
transliteration: triṃśadyojanakstīrṇā śatayojanamāyatā | svarṇaprākārasaṃvītā hematoraṇasaṃvṛtā || 7.5.25 ||
translation: त्रिंशत् thirty, योजनक्स् yojanas, तीर्णा wide, शतयोजनम् a hundred yojanas, आयता long, स्वर्णप्राकारसंवीता surrounded by golden walls, हेमतोरणसंवृता adorned with golden archways.
explanation: This place is thirty yojanas wide and a hundred yojanas long, surrounded by golden walls and adorned with golden archways.

shloka_text: मया लङ्केति नगरी शक्राज्ञप्तेन निर्मिता । तस्यां वसत दुर्धर्षा यूयं राक्षसपुङ्गवाः ।। 7.5.26 ।।
transliteration: mayā laṅketi nagarī śakrājñaptena nirmitā | tasyāṃ vasata durdharṣā yūyaṃ rākṣasapuṅgavāḥ || 7.5.26 ||
translation: मया by me, लङ्का Lanka, इति thus, नगरी city, शक्राज्ञप्तेन by Indra's command, निर्मिता built, तस्यां in that, वसत dwell, दुर्धर्षाः O invincible ones, यूयं you, राक्षसपुङ्गवाः O foremost Rakshasas.
explanation: This city, named Lanka, was built by me at Indra's command; O invincible and foremost Rakshasas, you should dwell there.

shloka_text: अमरावतीं समासाद्य सेन्द्रा इव दिवौकसः । लङ्कादुर्गं समासाद्य राक्षसैर्बहुभिर्वृताः ।। 7.5.27 ।।
transliteration: amarāvatīṃ samāsādya sendrā iva divaukasaḥ | laṅkādurgaṃ samāsādya rākṣasairbahubhirvṛtāḥ || 7.5.27 ||
translation: अमरावतीं Amaravati, समासाद्य having reached, सेन्द्राः with Indra, इव like, दिवौकसः gods, लङ्कादुर्गं the fortress of Lanka, समासाद्य having reached, राक्षसैः by Rakshasas, बहुभिः many, वृताः surrounded.
explanation: Having reached the fortress of Lanka, you will be surrounded by many Rakshasas, just as the gods, led by Indra, dwell in Amaravati.

shloka_text: भविष्यथ दुराधर्षाः शत्रूणां शत्रुसूदनाः ।। 7.5.28 ।।
transliteration: bhaviṣyatha durādharṣāḥ śatrūṇāṃ śatrusūdanāḥ || 7.5.28 ||
translation: भविष्यथ you will become, दुराधर्षाः invincible, शत्रूणां of enemies, शत्रुसूदनाः destroyers of enemies.
explanation: You will become invincible and destroyers of your enemies.

shloka_text: विश्वकर्मवचः श्रुत्वा ततस्ते राक्षसोत्तमाः । सहस्रानुचरा भूत्वा गत्वा तामवसन्पुरीम् ।। 7.5.29 ।।
transliteration: viśvakarmavacaḥ śrutvā tataste rākṣasottamāḥ | sahasrānucarā bhūtvā gatvā tāmavasanpurīm || 7.5.29 ||
translation: विश्वकर्मवचः the words of Vishwakarma, श्रुत्वा having heard, ततः then, ते those, राक्षसोत्तमाः best of Rakshasas, सहस्रानुचराः with thousands of followers, भूत्वा having become, गत्वा having gone, ताम् that, अवसन् dwelt, पुरीम् city.
explanation: Having heard the words of Vishwakarma, those foremost Rakshasas then went to that city with thousands of followers and dwelt there.

shloka_text: दृढप्राकारपरिखां हैमैर्गृहशतैर्वृताम् । लङ्कामवाप्य ते हृष्टा न्यवसन्रजनीचराः ।। 7.5.30 ।।
transliteration: dṛḍhaprākāraparikhāṃ haimairgṛhaśatairvṛtām | laṅkāmavāpya te hṛṣṭā nyavasanrajanīcarāḥ || 7.5.30 ||
translation: दृढप्राकारपरिखां with strong walls and moats, हैमैः golden, गृहशतैः by hundreds of houses, वृताम् surrounded, लङ्कां Lanka, अवाप्य having obtained, ते those, हृष्टाः delighted, न्यवसन् dwelt, रजनीचराः night-wanderers (Rakshasas).
explanation: Having obtained Lanka, which was surrounded by strong walls and moats and hundreds of golden houses, those delighted night-wanderers (Rakshasas) took up residence there.

shloka_text: एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु यथाकामं च राघव । नर्मदा नाम गन्धर्वी बभूव रघुनन्दन ।। 7.5.31 ।।
transliteration: etasminneva kāle tu yathākāmaṃ ca rāghava | narmadā nāma gandharvī babhūva raghunandana || 7.5.31 ||
translation: एतस्मिन् in this, एव indeed, काले time, तु and, यथाकामं as desired, च and, राघव O Raghava, नर्मदा Narmada, नाम named, गन्धर्वी a Gandharva woman, बभूव was born, रघुनन्दन O delight of Raghu's lineage.
explanation: O Raghava, O delight of Raghu's lineage, at this very time, a Gandharva woman named Narmada was born as desired.

shloka_text: तस्याः कान्यात्रयं ह्यासीत् धीश्रीकिर्तिसमद्युति । ज्येष्ठक्रमेण सा तेषां राक्षसानामराक्षसी ।। 7.5.32 ।।
transliteration: tasyāḥ kānyātrayaṃ hyāsīt dhīśrīkirtisamadyuti | jyeṣṭhakrameṇa sā teṣāṃ rākṣasānāmarākṣasī || 7.5.32 ||
translation: तस्याः her, कान्यात्रयम् three daughters, हि indeed, आसीत् were, धीश्रीकिर्तिसमद्युति having splendor equal to intellect, prosperity, and fame, ज्येष्ठक्रमेण in order of seniority, सा she, तेषाम् of them, राक्षसानाम् of the Rākṣasas, अराक्षसी not a Rākṣasī.
explanation: She, who was not a Rākṣasī, indeed had three daughters whose splendor was equal to intellect, prosperity, and fame, and these daughters were for those Rākṣasas in order of their seniority.

shloka_text: कन्यास्ताः प्रददौ हृष्टा पूर्णचन्द्रनिभाननाः । त्रयाणां राक्षसेन्द्राणां तिस्रो गन्धर्वकन्यकाः ।। 7.5.33 ।।
transliteration: kanyāstāḥ pradadau hṛṣṭā pūrṇacandranibhānanāḥ | trayāṇāṃ rākṣasendrāṇāṃ tisro gandharvakanyakāḥ || 7.5.33 ||
translation: कन्याः daughters, ताः those, प्रददौ gave, हृष्टा delighted, पूर्णचन्द्रनिभाननाः having faces like the full moon, त्रयाणाम् to the three, राक्षसेन्द्राणाम् chiefs of Rākṣasas, तिस्रः three, गन्धर्वकन्यकाः Gandharva maidens.
explanation: Delighted, she gave those three Gandharva maidens, whose faces resembled the full moon, to the three chiefs of the Rākṣasas.

shloka_text: दत्ता मात्रा महाभागा नक्षत्रे भगदैवते । कुतदारास्तु ते राम सुकेशतनयास्तदा ।। 7.5.34 ।।
transliteration: dattā mātrā mahābhāgā nakṣatre bhagadaivate | kutadārāstu te rāma sukeśatanayāstadā || 7.5.34 ||
translation: दत्ता given, मात्रा by the mother, महाभागा O greatly fortunate one, नक्षत्रे in the constellation, भगदैवते presided over by Bhaga, कुतदाराः having taken wives, तु indeed, ते those, राम O Rama, सुकेशतनयाः sons of Sukesha, तदा then.
explanation: O greatly fortunate Rama, those sons of Sukesha then indeed took wives, given by their mother in the constellation presided over by Bhaga.

shloka_text: चिक्रीडुः सह भार्याभिरप्सरोभिरिवामराः । ततो माल्यवतो भार्या सुन्दरी नाम सुन्दरी ।। 7.5.35 ।।
transliteration: cikrīḍuḥ saha bhāryābhirapsarobhirivāmarāḥ | tato mālyavato bhāryā sundarī nāma sundarī || 7.5.35 ||
translation: चिक्रीडुः they sported, सह with, भार्याभिः their wives, अप्सरोभिः with Apsaras, इव like, अमराः gods, ततः then, माल्यवतः of Malyavan, भार्या wife, सुन्दरी Sundari, नाम named, सुन्दरी beautiful.
explanation: They sported with their wives like gods with Apsaras; then, Malyavan's wife, named Sundari, who was beautiful...

shloka_text: स तस्यां जनयामास यदपत्यं निबोध तत् । वज्रमुष्टिर्विरूपाक्षोदुर्मुखश्चैव राक्षसः ।। 7.5.36 ।।
transliteration: sa tasyāṃ janayāmāsa yadapatyaṃ nibodha tat | vajramuṣṭirvirūpākṣodurmukhaścaiva rākṣasaḥ || 7.5.36 ||
translation: सः he, तस्याम् in her, जनयामास begot, यत् what, अपत्यम् offspring, निबोध know, तत् that, वज्रमुष्टिः Vajramushti, विरूपाक्षः Virupaksha, दुर्मुखः Durmukha, च and, एव indeed, राक्षसः Rākṣasa.
explanation: He begot in her the following offspring: Vajramushti, Virupaksha, and Durmukha, who were Rākṣasas.

shloka_text: सुप्तघ्नो यज्ञकोपश्च मत्तोन्मत्तौ तथैव च । अनला चाभवत्कन्या सुन्दर्यां राम सुन्दरी ।। 7.5.37 ।।
transliteration: suptaghno yajñakopaśca mattonmattau tathaiva ca | analā cābhavatkanyā sundaryāṃ rāma sundarī || 7.5.37 ||
translation: सुप्तघ्नो Suptaghna, यज्ञकोपश्च and Yajñakopa, मत्तोन्मत्तौ Matta and Unmatta, तथैव ca and similarly, अनला Anala, च and, अभवत् was born, कन्या a daughter, सुन्दर्यां from Sundari, राम O Rama, सुन्दरी a beautiful one
explanation: O Rama, from Sundari were born sons named Suptaghna, Yajñakopa, Matta, and Unmatta, and also a beautiful daughter named Anala.

shloka_text: सुमालिनो ऽपि भार्यासीत्पूर्णचद्रनिभानना । नाम्ना केतुमती राम प्राणेभ्यो ऽपि गरीयसी ।। 7.5.38 ।।
transliteration: sumālino 'pi bhāryāsītpūrṇacadranibhānanā | nāmnā ketumatī rāma prāṇebhyo 'pi garīyasī || 7.5.38 ||
translation: सुमालिनो of Sumali, अपि also, भार्या a wife, आसीत् was, पूर्णचद्रनिभानना with a face like the full moon, नाम्ना by name, केतुमती Ketumati, राम O Rama, प्राणेभ्यो than life, अपि even, गरीयसी dearer
explanation: O Rama, Sumali also had a wife named Ketumati, whose face was like the full moon and who was dearer to him than his own life.

shloka_text: सुमाली जनयामास यदपत्यं निशाचरः । केतुमत्यां महाराज तन्निबोधानुपूर्वशः ।। 7.5.39 ।।
transliteration: sumālī janayāmāsa yadapatyaṃ niśācaraḥ | ketumatyāṃ mahārāja tannibodhānupūrvaśaḥ || 7.5.39 ||
translation: सुमाली Sumali, जनयामास begot, यदपत्यं what offspring, निशाचरः the night-wanderer, केतुमत्यां in Ketumati, महाराज O great king, तत् that, निबोध know, अनुपूर्वशः in due order
explanation: O great king, now learn in due order about the offspring that the demon Sumali begot through Ketumati.

shloka_text: प्रहस्तो ऽकम्पनश्चैव विकटः कालकार्मुखः । धूम्राक्षश्चैव दण्डश्च सुपार्श्वश्च महाबलः ।। 7.5.40 ।।
transliteration: prahasto 'kampanaścaiva vikaṭaḥ kālakārmukhaḥ | dhūmrākṣaścaiva daṇḍaśca supārśvaśca mahābalaḥ || 7.5.40 ||
translation: प्रहस्तो Prahasta, अकम्पनश्चैव and Akampana, विकटः Vikata, कालकार्मुखः Kalakarmukha, धूम्राक्षश्चैव and Dhūmrākṣa, दण्डश्च and Danda, सुपार्श्वश्च and Suparshva, महाबलः the mighty
explanation: These sons were Prahasta, Akampana, Vikata, Kalakarmukha, Dhūmrākṣa, Danda, and the mighty Suparshva.

shloka_text: संह्रादिः प्रघसश्चैव भासकर्णश्च राक्षसः । राका पुष्पोत्कटा चैव कैकसी च शुचिस्मिता ।। कुम्भीनसी च इत्येते सुमालेः प्रसवाः स्मृताः ।। 7.5.41 ।।
transliteration: saṃhrādiḥ praghasaścaiva bhāsakarṇaśca rākṣasaḥ | rākā puṣpotkaṭā caiva kaikasī ca śucismitā || kumbhīnasī ca ityete sumāleḥ prasavāḥ smṛtāḥ || 7.5.41 ||
translation: संह्रादिः Samhradi, प्रघसश्चैव and Praghasa, भासकर्णश्च and Bhasakarna, राक्षसः the demon, राका Raka, पुष्पोत्कटा Pushpotkata, चैव and, कैकसी Kaikasi, च and, शुचिस्मिता with a pure smile, कुम्भीनसी Kumbhinasi, च and, इत्येते these, सुमालेः of Sumali, प्रसवाः offspring, स्मृताः are known
explanation: The demon's other offspring were Samhradi, Praghasa, Bhasakarna, Raka, Pushpotkata, Kaikasi of the pure smile, and Kumbhinasi, all known as Sumali's progeny.

shloka_text: कुम्भीनसी च इत्येते सुमालेः प्रसवाः स्मृताः ।। 7.5.41 ।।
transliteration: kumbhīnasī ca ityete sumāleḥ prasavāḥ smṛtāḥ || 7.5.41 ||
translation: कुम्भीनसी Kumbhinasi, च and, इत्येते these, सुमालेः of Sumali, प्रसवाः offspring, स्मृताः are known।
explanation: Kumbhinasi and others are known as the offspring of Sumali.

shloka_text: मालेस्तु वसुधा नाम गन्धर्वी रूपशालिनी । भार्यासीत्पद्मपत्राक्षी स्वक्षी यक्षीवरोपमा ।। 7.5.42 ।।
transliteration: mālestu vasudhā nāma gandharvī rūpaśālinī | bhāryāsītpadmapatrākṣī svakṣī yakṣīvaropamā || 7.5.42 ||
translation: मालेः Of Mali, तु indeed, वसुधा Vasudha, नाम named, गन्धर्वी a Gandharva woman, रूपशालिनी beautiful, भार्या wife, आसीत् was, पद्मपत्राक्षी lotus-leaf-eyed, स्वक्षी beautiful-eyed, यक्षीवरोपमा resembling the best of Yakshinis।
explanation: Mali's wife was a beautiful Gandharva woman named Vasudha, who had eyes like lotus petals and was as splendid as a chief Yakshini.

shloka_text: सुमालेरनुजस्तस्यां जनयामास यत् प्रभो । अपत्यं कथ्यमानं तु मया त्वं शृणु राघव ।। 7.5.43 ।।
transliteration: sumāleranujastasyāṃ janayāmāsa yat prabho | apatyaṃ kathyamānaṃ tu mayā tvaṃ śṛṇu rāghava || 7.5.43 ||
translation: सुमालेः Of Sumali, अनुजः the younger brother, तस्यां in her, जनयामास begot, यत् what, प्रभो O Lord, अपत्यं offspring, कथ्यमानं being told, तु indeed, मया by me, त्वं you, शृणु listen, राघव O Raghava।
explanation: O Lord Raghava, listen to the offspring that Sumali's younger brother begot in her, which I am now relating to you.

shloka_text: अनिलश्चानलश्चैव हरः सम्पातिरेव च । एते विभीषणामात्या मालेयास्तु निशाचरः ।। 7.5.44 ।।
transliteration: anilaścānalaścaiva haraḥ sampātireva ca | ete vibhīṣaṇāmātyā māleyāstu niśācaraḥ || 7.5.44 ||
translation: अनिलः Anila, च and, अनलः Anala, च and, एव indeed, हरः Hara, सम्पातिः Sampati, एव indeed, च and, एते these, विभीषणामात्याः ministers of Vibhishana, मालेयाः sons of Mali, तु indeed, निशाचरः night-wanderers।
explanation: Anila, Anala, Hara, and Sampati are these sons of Mali, who were night-wanderers and later became ministers of Vibhishana.

shloka_text: ततस्तु ते राक्षसपुङ्गवास्त्रयो निशाचरैः पुत्रशतैश्च संवृताः । सुरान्सहेन्द्रानृषिनागयक्षान्बबाधिरे तान्बहुवीर्यदर्पिताः ।। 7.5.45 ।।
transliteration: tatastu te rākṣasapuṅgavāstrayo niśācaraiḥ putraśataiśca saṃvṛtāḥ | surānsahendrānṛṣināgayakṣānbabādhire tānbahuvīryadarpitāḥ || 7.5.45 ||
translation: ततः Then, तु indeed, ते those, राक्षसपुङ्गवाः chief Rakshasas, त्रयः three, निशाचरैः by night-wanderers, पुत्रशतैः by hundreds of sons, च and, संवृताः surrounded, सुरान् the gods, सहेन्द्रान् along with Indra, ऋषिनागयक्षान् the Rishis, Nagas, and Yakshas, बबाधिरे tormented, तान् them, बहुवीर्यदर्पिताः arrogant with great power।
explanation: Then, those three chief Rakshasas, surrounded by hundreds of their Rakshasa sons, became arrogant with their immense power and tormented the gods along with Indra, as well as the Rishis, Nagas, and Yakshas.

shloka_text: जगद्भ्रमन्तो ऽनिलवद्दुरासदा रणेषु मृत्युप्रतिमानतेजसः । वरप्रदानादतिगर्विता भृशं क्रतुक्रियाणां प्रशमङ्कराः सदा ।। 7.5.46 ।।
transliteration: jagadbhramanto 'nilavaddurāsadā raṇeṣu mṛtyupratimānatejasaḥ | varapradānādatigarvitā bhṛśaṃ kratukriyāṇāṃ praśamaṅkarāḥ sadā || 7.5.46 ||
translation: जगत् world, भ्रमन्तः wandering, अनिलवत् like wind, दुरासदा difficult to approach, रणेषु in battles, मृत्युप्रतिमानतेजसः having valor equal to death, वरप्रदानात् due to the boon, अतिगर्विताः extremely proud, भृशम् exceedingly, क्रतुक्रियाणाम् of sacrificial rites, प्रशमङ्कराः destroyers, सदा always.
explanation: These beings wander the world like the wind, are difficult to approach, possess valor equal to death in battles, are exceedingly proud due to the boon they received, and always destroy sacrificial rites. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे पञ्चमः सर्गः ।। 5 ।। Thus ends the fifth sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
